explanation: Sound moves at about 343 metres a second in air, about 1,480 in water and roughly 5,000 or more in steel. Stiffer materials pass vibrations along faster.

claims.text: Of steel, water, air and helium, sound travels fastest through steel.
Sound travels more slowly in water, air and helium than in steel.
Sound travels at about 343 m/s in air at 20 °C.
Sound travels at about 1,480 m/s in water.
Sound travels at roughly 5,000 m/s or more in steel.
Sound generally travels faster in stiffer materials.
